routes.description: Establish a cumulative route from features of the universe, objective morality, the historical case for resurrection, and religious experience to a personal God, then connect that conclusion to Christian theism while answering objections from suffering and religion's record.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its independent considerations jointly make a personal God more plausible than atheistic naturalism, the resurrection consideration supplies the specifically Christian bridge, and the principal defeaters do not overturn that cumulative inference.

motionBridge.description: Show that the cumulative explanatory case and specifically Christian evidence make Christian theism more plausible than atheism across the motion's principal issues.

centralBridges.description: Establish that cosmic origin and life-permitting conditions are better explained by a transcendent personal cause and intelligent design than by necessity, chance, or unaided naturalism.
Establish that objective moral values and duties require a transcendent foundation that theism supplies and atheistic accounts do not.
Establish that the relevant historical facts are best explained by Jesus's resurrection and that this inference connects generic theism to Christian theism.
Show that suffering, evolutionary waste, religious plurality, and harmful religious conduct do not defeat the truth or comparative plausibility of Christian theism.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain how public arguments may be supplemented by immediate religious experience without making the public cumulative case depend solely on private assurance.
Account for objective meaning, providential justice, and redemption within Christian theism, including for suffering people and those outside explicit Christian history.

routes.description: Withhold the divine hypothesis unless it receives adequate evidential support, challenge the inferences from cosmic and moral phenomena to God, resist the further bridge to Christianity, and present suffering, religious plurality, and religion's authoritative record as contrary considerations.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the affirmative considerations neither require a divine explanation nor establish the caring and specifically Christian God at issue, while the counterevidence and secular alternatives leave atheistic rejection of that hypothesis warranted.

motionBridge.description: Show that the available considerations do not warrant the divine hypothesis or the further conclusion that a caring, revelatory, specifically Christian God exists.

centralBridges.description: Defend rejection of an unsupported supernatural proposition without assuming an obligation to prove the nonexistence of every proposed deity.
Show that cosmological uncertainty, evolutionary contingency, and secular accounts of morality prevent the relevant phenomena from requiring design or divine moral grounding.
Show that a possible cosmic cause would not establish providence or Christianity and that miracle testimony does not adequately authenticate resurrection, revelation, or doctrine.
Show that severe suffering, cosmic and evolutionary waste, delayed and unequal revelation, and conflicting religions count against benevolent Christian providence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why claims of divine authority demand strong evidence and why scriptural commands and theocratic coercion bear on accepting those claims.
Establish that human solidarity, freedom, ethical life, and meaningful projects remain available without supernatural authority or immortality.

sections.title: Burden of Proof and Religious Epistemology
sections.rationale: The parties' competing accounts of atheism, evidential obligation, cumulative probability, falsifiability, and spiritual assurance determine what must be established before any substantive consideration can support or displace the divine hypothesis.

sections.title: Cosmic Origin, Fine-Tuning, and Design
sections.rationale: Cosmological origin and fine-tuning form a principal route from observable features of the universe to a personal creator, while uncertainty, evolutionary contingency, waste, and cosmic decay test whether that explanatory inference is warranted.

sections.title: Objective Morality and Its Foundation
sections.rationale: The moral issue tests whether objective values and duties require God, whether evolutionary and social accounts address grounding or only moral development, and whether religious authority contributes anything necessary to ethical life.

sections.title: Resurrection, Miracles, and the Christian Bridge
sections.rationale: The resurrection claim supplies the principal bridge from generic creator theism to Christianity, making the historical facts, miracle testimony, doctrinal authentication, and the scope and timing of revelation structurally indispensable.

sections.title: Suffering, Evil, and Benevolent Providence
sections.rationale: Suffering and apparent waste directly test the compatibility and comparative plausibility of an omnipotent, knowledgeable, and good God, including whether sufficient reasons, redemption, and eternal compensation answer the objection.

sections.title: Religion's Record, Authority, and Human Meaning
sections.rationale: Religion's commands and institutional consequences bear on claims of revelation and authority, while the competing accounts of objective purpose, secular solidarity, liberty, and mortality address the motion's broader contrast between Christian theism and atheism.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: Atheism lacks a successful argument establishing that God does not exist.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: The universe began to exist and therefore has a transcendent personal cause.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Cosmic fine-tuning is best explained by intelligent design rather than necessity or chance.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Objective moral values exist, and their existence entails that God exists.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: The best explanation of the central historical facts about Jesus is his resurrection, which entails God's existence.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Immediate experience of God can properly ground knowledge of God's existence without inferential argument.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-04.proposition: A worldview's truth cannot be inferred from its beneficial or harmful social consequences, so the debate should turn on arguments for truth rather than comparative death tolls.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-05.proposition: On atheism human existence can have subjective projects but no objective purpose, whereas fellowship with God provides humanity's true fulfillment and enduring meaning.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-07.proposition: Neither the logical nor probabilistic problem of evil defeats theism, and Christianity addresses suffering through God's sufficient reasons, Christ's suffering, and hope of eternal life.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Evolutionary mass extinction, randomness, suffering, and humanity's near extinction undermine the claim that humanity was the intended product of a purposeful divine design.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Atheism need not prove God's nonexistence when no plausible or convincing evidence requires the divine hypothesis and observable phenomena remain explicable without it.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: Even granting a cosmic creator would not establish a caring, intervening, revelatory, salvific, or specifically Christian God.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Giving inner spiritual assurance precedence over contrary argument or evidence insulates Christian commitment from evidential defeat and makes the apologetic fundamentally faith-based.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: Severe cosmological uncertainty, explanatory regress, failed cosmic structures, destruction, and eventual extinction count against inferring competent benevolent design from fine-tuning.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Humanity's long prehistoric suffering and Christianity's late, uneven, and conflicting transmission undermine claims of benevolent providential design and universal redemption.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Human moral capacities arise from social solidarity and predate monotheism, while religious sanction contributes no uniquely moral action and can motivate distinctive harms.

chunk-003:c003-04.proposition: Even if suspensions of natural law or miracles occur, miraculous performance alone does not establish the truth of the performer's doctrine or divine identity.

chunk-003:c003-10.proposition: Treating religions as human creations explains their plurality, while justice, love, duty, and other ethical problems remain human concerns that do not require celestial authority.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-03.proposition: Religion's harmful record bears on its authority when scriptures specifically command atrocities, unlike scientific discoveries that can be misused without themselves constituting an ideology.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-06.proposition: Human freedom and solidarity can make mortal life meaningful without immortality, while purported religious authority can obstruct liberty in this world.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-08.proposition: A theism that renders prolonged unanswered abuse worthwhile through later compensation can absorb any horror into divine purpose and make the abuser an instrument of providence.
